record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: How do tachyonic-instability-induced friction and thermal friction interact when both are available in an axion-gauge-field system, which mechanism turns on first, and how should one model the nonlinear evolution and initial conditions of the later stage?

evidence.quote: Interesting interplay exists between friction caused by tachyonic instabilities [236, 237] and thermal friction [238, 239].
One mechanism can precede the other, setting the initial conditions for thermal friction to take over [240].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an axion field $\phi$ with decay constant $f$ coupled to a non-Abelian (or Abelian) gauge field $A_\mu$ with field strength $F_{\mu
u}$ and dual $	ilde F^{\mu
u}$, through the Chern–Simons interaction $\mathcal{L}_{m int} =  rac{\alpha}{4f}\,\phi\, F_{\mu
u}	ilde F^{\mu
u}$, in an expanding FRW background with Hubble rate $H$ and ambient radiation temperature $T$. The motion of $\phi$ is subject to two distinct dissipative mechanisms:

(i) Tachyonic-instability-induced friction: when $\dot\phi/f$ exceeds a critical value, one polarization of the gauge field develops an exponentially growing (tachyonic) mode that backreacts on $\phi$, producing an effective friction term $\Upsilon_{m tach}(\dot\phi, H)\,\dot\phi$ in the equation of motion.

(ii) Thermal friction: in the presence of a thermal bath of gauge quanta with temperature $T$, sphaleron-like processes induce a friction term $\Upsilon_{m th}(T)\,\dot\phi$, typically $\Upsilon_{m th}\propto T^3/f^2$ (with appropriate coupling-dependent prefactors).

Problem. Within the coupled system
$$\ddot\phi + 3H\dot\phi +  ig(\Upsilon_{m tach}(\dot\phi,H) + \Upsilon_{m th}(T) ig)\dot\phi + V'(\phi) = 0,$$
together with the gauge-field mode equations and the radiation energy-density equation sourced by both friction channels:

(a) Determine, as a function of the model parameters $(\alpha, f, V, H, T)$ and initial data, which of the two friction mechanisms activates first along the cosmological evolution.

(b) Characterize the nonlinear backreaction regime of the tachyonic phase, including the saturation amplitude of the produced gauge quanta and the resulting effective $\Upsilon_{m tach}$.

(c) Derive the matching conditions (initial conditions for $\phi$, $\dot\phi$, gauge-field spectra, and radiation temperature) under which the tachyonic phase hands over to the thermal-friction phase, and formulate a consistent effective description that smoothly interpolates between the two regimes.
artifact.status_search_result: The interplay between tachyonic (gauge-field amplification) friction and thermal (sphaleron) friction in axion–gauge systems remains an active area of research in cosmology and axion inflation/warm inflation, with no complete nonlinear treatment establishing a unified framework. Recent literature continues to investigate backreaction regimes and matching between the two stages.
